result.summary: This agreement sets out the terms for Alex Morgan to design and build a customer website for Northwind Digital Ltd starting on 1 October 2026. It grants the Client ownership of all work product and pre-existing materials upon creation, and includes strict confidentiality, worldwide non-compete, and unlimited liability clauses. The contract also contains contradictory payment terms and allows the Client to change terms or terminate the agreement at any time.

quote.text: This Agreement is made on 1 October 2026 between Northwind Digital Ltd ("the Client") and Alex Morgan ("the Contractor

key_terms.label: Fees
key_terms.value: Amounts set out in Schedule A

quote.text: Fees" means the amounts set out in Schedule A
This Agreement lasts for twelve (12) months and renews automatically for further twelve-month periods unless either party gives notice
This Agreement is governed by the laws of England and Wales

risks.title: Unlimited Liability and Indemnity
risks.plain_language: The contractor is held liable for all losses suffered by the client without limit, and must indemnify the client against any third-party claims relating to the deliverables.
risks.why_it_matters: A single mistake or dispute could cost you far more than you earn from the contract, as there is no cap on your financial exposure.

quotes.text: The Contractor is liable for all losses suffered by the Client arising from the Services, without limit
The Contractor will indemnify the Client against any claim by a third party relating to the Deliverables

risks.title: Worldwide Non-Compete
risks.plain_language: For 24 months after the agreement ends, the contractor cannot provide services to any competing business anywhere in the world.
risks.why_it_matters: This restriction is extremely broad geographically and could severely limit your ability to find work in your industry after finishing this project.

quotes.text: For twenty-four (24) months after this Agreement ends, the Contractor will not provide services to any business that competes with the Client anywhere in the world

risks.title: Assignment of Pre-Existing Materials and IP
risks.plain_language: All rights in the deliverables, including drafts, source files, and any pre-existing materials owned by the contractor before the agreement, are assigned to the client immediately upon creation.
risks.why_it_matters: You lose ownership of your background tools, templates, and pre-existing assets used in the project, and you are barred from showing the work in your portfolio without written consent.

quotes.text: All rights in the Deliverables, including any pre-existing materials of the Contractor used in them, are assigned to the Client on creation
The Contractor may not show the Deliverables in a portfolio without the Client's prior written consent

risks.title: One-Sided Termination and Payment Risk
risks.plain_language: The client can terminate the agreement immediately at any time and pay only for deliverables it has accepted, while the contractor must give 90 days' notice. Furthermore, the client may withhold payment if not satisfied.
risks.why_it_matters: The client can walk away at any moment and refuse payment based on subjective dissatisfaction, leaving you unpaid for completed work.

quotes.text: The Client may withhold any payment if it is not satisfied with the Deliverables
The Client may terminate this Agreement at any time with immediate effect. The Contractor may terminate on ninety (90) days' written notice
On termination the Client will pay only for Deliverables it has accepted

risks.title: Unilateral Agreement Changes
risks.plain_language: The client can update the agreement terms at any time by posting a new version on its portal, and the contractor's continued work constitutes acceptance.
risks.why_it_matters: The client can alter your pay, obligations, or rights without your direct consent simply by updating a webpage.

quotes.text: The Client may update these terms by posting a new version on its supplier portal. Continued work by the Contractor means acceptance

risks.title: Binding Arbitration and Class-Action Waiver
risks.plain_language: Any dispute must be resolved through binding arbitration in London, and the contractor waives the right to bring or join a class or collective action.
risks.why_it_matters: You give up your right to go to court and your ability to join forces with other contractors if a systemic dispute arises.

quotes.text: Any dispute will be resolved by binding arbitration in London. The Contractor waives any right to bring or join a class or collective action

inconsistencies: Section 3.1 states payment is due within ninety (90) days of receiving an invoice, while Section 3.4 states each invoice is payable within thirty (30) days of receipt.
missing_or_unclear: Schedule A containing the Fees is missing.
The notice period required to prevent automatic renewal under Section 8.1 is undefined.
Acceptance criteria for the Deliverables are undefined, leaving satisfaction entirely to the Client's discretion.
questions_for_lawyer: Ask about Section 4.1: How can I protect my pre-existing background materials and retain portfolio rights?
Ask about Section 6.1 and 7.1: How can I negotiate a liability cap and narrow the worldwide non-compete clause?
Ask about Section 9.1: How can I protect myself against unilateral changes made via the supplier portal?
next_steps: Do not sign the agreement on Friday until these major risks and missing schedules are addressed.
Draft a list of requested amendments regarding liability caps, IP ownership of pre-existing materials, payment terms, and removal of the unilateral change clause.
Ask the Client to provide the missing Schedule A with the agreed fee structure.
Send your proposed changes to the Client in writing before agreeing to sign.
